context: dense process piping & alloy metallurgy · utilities-first commissioning

brief.intro: New to this project type? A chemical, petrochemical or refinery complex looks like an oil & gas facility but is denser and slower: more process piping per square metre, more exotic alloy metallurgy (which takes far longer to fabricate and weld than carbon steel), and heavy insulation and heat-tracing scope. The defining planning rule is that utilities — steam, nitrogen, instrument air, cooling water — must be built and proven before any process unit can be commissioned; the utility block is the gating milestone the whole plant waits on. The programme ends with catalyst loading and a staged, utility-first start-up rather than a single switch-on.

must_get_right: Utilities (steam, nitrogen, instrument air, cooling water) commission first — the utility block is the gating milestone for every process unit; protect its completion date above all others.
Alloy / exotic-metallurgy piping has a much longer fabrication and welding lead time than carbon steel — track it separately and flag it early.
Effluent/neutralization and the flare system are compliance-critical, not finishing items — protect their completion dates like any safety system.
Catalyst loading and reactor conditioning are late, sequenced, largely irreversible steps — hold real contingency immediately ahead of them.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Activities carry durations in working days; the network is calculated (F9) with no artificial constraints beyond contractual milestones. Total float is kept ≥ 0 in the baseline.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Civil and structural steel run a 6-day week; alloy piping fabrication and welding run to a coded-welder resource calendar rather than simple shifts; commissioning runs a 7-day calendar once the utility-first sequence begins.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: The driving path runs long-lead procurement (reactors, columns, exchangers) → heavy foundations → static equipment set → alloy and carbon-steel piping fabrication and erection → the utilities block built and commissioned first → DCS/SIS integration → catalyst loading → staged start-up. Utility-block readiness is the single gating milestone every process unit waits on.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Design and hazardous-area classification are frozen; permits and authority approvals are obtained per phase gate; a single mobilisation; and metallurgy selections (alloy vs carbon steel) are finalised before spool fabrication starts. Any change to these invalidates the baseline dates.

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Heavy lifts (reactors, columns, exchangers) require crane windows and hardstand; alloy welding needs coded welders and NDT technicians who are typically in short supply and a resource constraint on the piping front; hazardous-area work runs under a hot-work/cold-work permit system.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Principal risks: alloy piping slippage (fabrication and coded-welder availability), utility-block delay cascading into every downstream process unit, and the irreversible nature of catalyst loading. Schedule contingency is held immediately before utility-first commissioning and before catalyst loading rather than spread thinly across activities.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for the field — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
